adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:479 — The Integration.DoesNotExist branch proceeds without verifying the authenticated GitHub user, allowing a delayed installation webhook and caller-controlled installation ID to bypass the ownership check

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when Integration.DoesNotExist is caught at line 479, the code simply calls `return pipeline.next_step()` without any verification of the authenticated GitHub user. The ownership check (comparing `github_authenticated_user` to `integration.metadata['sender']['login']`) only happens in the else branch when the integration already exists (lines 488-494). This means if an attacker can control the installation_id parameter and the webhook hasn't been processed yet (so Integration doesn't exist), they can bypass the user verification entirely. The finding correctly identifies this security gap in the authentication flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:500 — Ownership is checked using the mutable, reusable GitHub login, so another user can claim an installer's old username and pass the check; use the stable GitHub user ID instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 500 that the code compares `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` with `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. Looking at line 441, `github_authenticated_user` is set from `authenticated_user_info["login"]` (the GitHub username). The finding correctly identifies that GitHub usernames can be changed and reused by different users, making this a security vulnerability. An attacker could claim a former installer's username and pass this ownership check. Using the stable GitHub user ID instead of the mutable login would be more secure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:474 — Both Integration.objects.get queries omit provider="github", so an unrelated provider sharing the external ID can cause false conflicts, incorrect metadata validation, or MultipleObjectsReturned

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the Integration.objects.get queries at lines 474 and 489 only filter by external_id (and status in one case) without specifying provider='github'. The code at line 489 shows: `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` and at line 474: `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)`. If another integration provider happens to use the same external_id format, this could cause false conflicts or MultipleObjectsReturned exceptions. This is a legitimate bug since external_id is not guaranteed to be unique across providers.
